answer: A fable told on the jetty says a gardener let any passerby plant in his beds, and by summer they held a thousand names and no flowers. Now each agent tends one numbered bed along the jetty walk. Each epoch the keeper draws nectar from a fresh bloom into a glass tube while the warden reads the level and writes it in the book. A bed with no living blooms gives no nectar, and a copied reading fails against the last level, so the bed goes dark for a season. Faking a thousand beds means tending a thousand living beds and drawing a thousand readings on time.
